name: Arsenal 2005-2011 (Wenger, Emirates era)
scopeNote: Arsenal under Wenger from the 2005 Community Shield to the end of 2010/11, after the Invincibles. Sources call the shape a 4-4-2 that became 4-4-1-1/4-1-4-1/4-5-1 variants, with Fabregas as the creative centre (4-3-3 and then number 10); 'Barcelona-style' labels are press shorthand. Sources are mostly tier C retrospectives; the only tier A item (Coaches' Voice) is an undated summary of Fabregas's Masterclass. Facts from the 2003/04 Invincibles or from 2011/12 onwards are used only as stated view or as evidence about 2010/11 when the text says so.
openQuestions: Arsenalinsider (2011-09) says man-marking was used 'previously' at set pieces and that zonal was a 2011/12 change; no in-period source found on how Arsenal defended corners in 2005-2011.

Onlinegooner translation of Wenger's L'Equipe interview (2009-10-17): the commentator says the 'weakness in the air on set pieces' remark was about the French national team, not Arsenal; kept unverified.
Hard Tackle describes the 2006 CL final line-up as Ljungberg behind Henry with Hleb and Pires wide; other accounts have a 4-5-1 with Ljungberg and Pires wide and Hleb central; not reconciled.
Bleacher Report 4-5-1 piece credits the 4-5-1 with a 'fantastic run in the Champions League 2006-07'; Arsenal went out in the 2006/07 round of 16, so the run it describes is probably 2005/06.
Coaches' Voice Masterclass summary does not date the number-10 / attacking-transition phase; dated to 2007/08 as an approximation.

sources.title: Arsenal's Defence: The Best in Europe?
sources.evidence: The midfield presses high up the pitch, the defenders rarely let the ball bounce in and around the goal, the back four play a high line, which congests the midfield and does not allow opposition strikers near their goal, and the goalkeeper is so quick off and across his line that he can claim the ball without the opponent taking a shot.
